epic.title: Pruning & Retention
epic.description: Implements spec section 15 Pruning and Retention: a primary-only (lease-enforced) pruning workflow that records signed pruning checkpoints (pruned_range = [start, end) at tree_size T), advances a replicated watermark, and removes leaf objects only after S3 Object Lock (Compliance mode) retention has expired. Includes the OQ-7 orchestration decision (Step Functions vs Lambda chain), pruning-worker Lambda plus CDK synth-tested infrastructure, configurable retention policy (default 7 years; pruning checkpoints retained indefinitely), and end-to-end LocalStack validation of Object Lock semantics, plus the mtcctl prune CLI/admin surface (spec 17.3), post-pruning fixture, pruning-failure runbook, and observability hooks. Revocation is a separate parallel epic (25.6) and is out of scope here.

tickets.title: ADR: resolve OQ-7 — Step Functions vs simple Lambda chain for pruning
tickets.description:
## Goal
Resolve OQ-7 (§26): choose Step Functions or a simple Lambda chain for the pruning workflow (§15.2, Phase 7 §24), recorded as an ADR that downstream tickets implement.

## Acceptance Criteria
- ADR committed under `docs/adr/` comparing both options on: LocalStack fidelity, retry/failure semantics, local debuggability, CDK complexity, agent-driven testability
- ADR ends with an explicit Decision and Consequences section naming the chosen mechanism unambiguously (no "either could work" hedging)
- Spike script checked in that executes a trivial state machine (or chained Lambda) against LocalStack, proving the chosen mechanism runs locally
- ADR restates the local-only constraint (§1 non-goals: no production cloud spend) and how the choice honors it

## Out of Scope
- Implementing the pruning workflow itself (prune-stepfn-workflow)
- CDK constructs (prune-cdk-workflow)

## Testing
- Spike integration check against LocalStack; no permanent test suite obligations beyond the committed spike script

## Demo
`make demo` env up, then run the spike script and show a successful execution in LocalStack logs.

tickets.title: PruningCheckpoint domain type, wire serialization, and fuzz target
tickets.description:
## Goal
Define the pruning checkpoint structure — a signed declaration of `pruned_range = [start, end) at tree_size T` (§15.2) — with newtype-based domain types (§22) and wire serialization.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `PruningCheckpoint` type: leaf-index range, tree_size, timestamp, signing key id; invalid ranges (start > end, end > tree_size) unconstructible or rejected on parse
- Serialize/parse implemented in the mtc wire-format style; `parse(serialize(x)) == x` round-trip property test (§19.2)
- Malformed input rejected without panic
- Fuzz target `fuzz/fuzz_targets/parse_pruning_checkpoint.rs` with seed corpus checked into `fuzz/corpus/` (§19.3); bug-finding inputs become regression fixtures

## Out of Scope
- Signing (prune-checkpoint-signer)
- Persistence/commit (prune-commit-protocol)

## Testing
- Unit, property (proptest round-trip), fuzz (cargo-fuzz)

## Demo
`cargo test -p mtc-core pruning_checkpoint` green; `cargo fuzz run parse_pruning_checkpoint -- -max_total_time=60` finds no crashes.

tickets.title: RetentionPolicy config: 7-year default, configurable, indefinite pruning checkpoints
tickets.description:
## Goal
Implement the retention policy configuration: default 7 years, configurable (§15.1); computes `retain_until` for entries/tiles/checkpoints; pruning checkpoints retained indefinitely (§15.3).

## Acceptance Criteria
- `RetentionPolicy` type parsed from service config with 7-year default; validation rejects zero/negative durations
- Helper computing `retain_until: SystemTime` for a given write time, used by ObjectLock `put_with_retention` call sites (§9.1)
- Pruning-checkpoint object class returns an indefinite/max sentinel retention
- Dev-mode override permitting short retention (minutes) so pruning is demoable on a laptop with the fake clock (§18.4)

## Out of Scope
- S3 lifecycle CDK rules (prune-cdk-lifecycle)
- Prunable-range computation (prune-planner)

## Testing
- Unit (boundary math, config parsing), property (retain_until monotonic in write time)

## Demo
`cargo test -p ca-pruning retention_policy`; demo env config shows short dev retention in `mtcctl status` output.

tickets.title: Pruning watermark item in coordination table with epoch-conditional writes
tickets.description:
## Goal
Extend the DDB coordination table with a `latest-pruning` SK item following the §8.2 item pattern (mirroring `latest-checkpoint`/`latest-revocation`): pruned_end, tree_size, s3_key, signed_at, epoch — written only with epoch condition (§8.3).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Storage facade methods to read and advance the watermark; advance includes `epoch` in ConditionExpression
- ConditionalCheckFailed surfaces as a typed lost-lease error (per §25.4 pattern)
- Watermark only moves forward; regression attempts rejected
- Memory backend parity: same behavior under `cloud-memory`
- Integration test against LocalStack DDB

## Out of Scope
- Commit sequence orchestration (prune-commit-protocol)
- CLI display (prune-cli-admin)

## Testing
- Unit (memory backend), integration (LocalStack DDB)

## Demo
After merge: in demo env, seed a watermark via test helper and read it back with a debug command showing the `latest-pruning` item.

tickets.title: Pruning planner: compute prunable range and object set honoring retention
tickets.description:
## Goal
Compute the candidate `pruned_range = [start, end)` and the exact set of leaf/entry objects eligible for deletion, given retention policy, injected clock, current watermark, and tree size (§15.2). Interior nodes are retained as needed via the tile structure.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Planner never includes an entry whose Object Lock retention (via `get_retention`, §9.1) has not expired
- Output range is well-formed: watermark <= start <= end <= tree_size; deterministic given inputs
- Object-key set covers only pruned leaf/entry objects; tiles required for inclusion proofs of unpruned entries are never listed (§15.2)
- Uses injected `Clock` (§18.4, §22.11) — no wall-clock reads

## Out of Scope
- Signing/commit (prune-commit-protocol); deletion (prune-deletion-executor)
- Proof-preservation property suite (prune-proof-property)

## Testing
- Unit, property (never prunes within retention window), Kani harness on range arithmetic (no overflow; well-formed range invariant)

## Demo
`cargo test -p ca-pruning planner`; dry-run helper prints planned range against a fixture tree.

tickets.title: Sign pruning checkpoints with dedicated HSM-backed pruning key
tickets.description:
## Goal
Sign `PruningCheckpoint` declarations with the dedicated pruning-checkpoint key (§14.1, ECDSA P-256 in v1) via the `Hsm` trait, reusing checkpoint-signer plumbing; pruning is never silent (§15.1).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Sign/verify functions for pruning checkpoints; signature verifies against the published pruning key
- Key id distinct from the log checkpoint signing key (§14.1 key table)
- Works against memory HSM and SoftHSM PKCS#11; SoftHSM path marked non-FIPS via `is_fips_validated()` (§14.4)
- Verification failure on tampered bytes covered by test

## Out of Scope
- Commit/persistence sequence (prune-commit-protocol)
- Key ceremony / rotation tooling (operational-tooling epic)

## Testing
- Unit (memory HSM backend), integration (SoftHSM via PKCS#11)

## Demo
In demo env: helper command signs a sample pruning declaration with SoftHSM and verifies it, printing the key id used.

tickets.title: Pruning commit sequence: sign, persist checkpoint, advance watermark (primary-only)
tickets.description:
## Goal
Implement the commit half of §15.2: plan -> sign -> persist pruning checkpoint to S3 with indefinite retention (§15.3) -> advance DDB watermark epoch-conditionally. Runs only on the primary (lease-enforced).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Checkpoint stored under the checkpoints prefix via `put_with_retention` with indefinite/max retention; bytes immutable thereafter (§8 invariants)
- Watermark advance uses epoch ConditionExpression; epoch bump mid-commit aborts cleanly with no watermark change
- Standby (non-leaseholder) refuses to run the commit
- No deletion performed in this step (deletion is a separate, later step)
- Pruning event record (range, tree_size, timestamp, operator/trigger) appended for the compliance Pruning log (§20.3)
- Retry after partial failure is idempotent

## Out of Scope
- Deletion executor (prune-deletion-executor); workflow orchestration (prune-stepfn-workflow)

## Testing
- Unit (memory backends), integration (LocalStack S3 + DDB), failure-injection test for mid-commit epoch bump

## Demo
Demo env: invoke commit step; show new pruning checkpoint object in LocalStack S3 and advanced `latest-pruning` item.

tickets.title: Deletion executor: remove pruned leaf objects only after Object Lock expiry
tickets.description:
## Goal
Implement the deletion step of §15.2: after the pruning checkpoint is committed and replicated, remove leaf/entry objects in the pruned range whose Object Lock retention has expired. §15.2/§8 designate S3 lifecycle as the production removal mechanism (prune-cdk-lifecycle); this executor is the workflow's explicit deletion pass so pruned state is deterministic, observable, and testable on LocalStack, and both must agree on eligibility.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Deletes only object keys from the planner's set, all below the committed watermark read from the `latest-pruning` item
- Replication precondition (§15.2 "after commit + replication") checked before any delete; configured no-op in single-region dev mode
- Objects with unexpired retention are skipped and reported, never force-deleted; Compliance-mode AccessDenied treated as an expected, non-fatal outcome (§15.3)
- Tiles needed for proofs of unpruned entries are never deleted; pruning checkpoints never deleted (§15.3)
- Partial-failure resume: re-running completes remaining deletes without error

## Out of Scope
- Workflow orchestration/scheduling (prune-stepfn-workflow)
- Lifecycle CDK rules (prune-cdk-lifecycle)

## Testing
- Unit (memory backend), integration (LocalStack Object Lock: delete refused before retain-until, succeeds after)

## Demo
Demo env with short dev retention: run executor; `awslocal s3api list-objects` shows pruned entries gone, tiles and checkpoints intact.

tickets.title: Pruning workflow orchestration (Step Functions per ADR) + pruning-worker Lambda
tickets.description:
## Goal
Orchestrate plan -> commit -> delete as the pruning workflow (Phase 7 §24; §7 pruning-worker Lambda), per the OQ-7 ADR decision, runnable end-to-end on LocalStack.

## Acceptance Criteria
- State machine (or Lambda chain per ADR) definition wiring planner, commit protocol, and deletion executor as steps with retries and terminal failure states
- `pruning-worker` Lambda handler binary in the workspace invoking the shared crates
- Scheduled trigger (EventBridge) with fast dev cadence; manual trigger supported
- Workflow no-ops safely when lease not held or nothing is prunable
- Execution observable in LocalStack (status queryable per execution)

## Out of Scope
- CDK constructs and synth assertions (prune-cdk-workflow)
- CLI trigger (prune-cli-admin)

## Testing
- Integration (LocalStack Step Functions execution happy path + failure-state path), unit for handler input/output shapes

## Demo
`make demo`, then start an execution via `awslocal stepfunctions start-execution` and watch it advance the watermark shown in the admin API.

tickets.title: CDK constructs for pruning workflow: state machine, Lambda, schedule (synth-only)
tickets.description:
## Goal
Add CDK (TypeScript) constructs for the pruning workflow: state machine, pruning-worker Lambda, and EventBridge schedule (§5, §7), validated by `cdk synth` assertions only (§1 non-goals: no cloud deploy).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Constructs added to the CDK app matching the OQ-7 ADR decision
- Synth assertion tests verify: state machine states/retry config, Lambda runtime + env wiring, schedule rule targeting the workflow
- Least-privilege IAM statements asserted (workflow can only touch log bucket prefixes and coordination table)
- No test requires AWS credentials or network

## Out of Scope
- S3 lifecycle and Object Lock bucket config (prune-cdk-lifecycle)
- Workflow runtime logic (prune-stepfn-workflow)

## Testing
- CDK synth assertion tests (Jest) in the infra package; runs in CI unit lane

## Demo
`npm test` in the CDK package green; `cdk synth` emits the pruning state machine and Lambda in the template.

tickets.title: CDK: S3 lifecycle + Object Lock Compliance config aligned with retention policy (synth-only)
tickets.description:
## Goal
Encode §8 and §15.3 storage invariants in CDK: Object Lock in Compliance mode, lifecycle rules that delete pruned leaf objects only after retention expiry (§8 S3 invariants, §15.2), CRR preserving Object Lock attributes — all validated via `cdk synth` assertions.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Synth assertions: bucket has Object Lock enabled in Compliance mode with default retention matching `RetentionPolicy` (7 years)
- Lifecycle expiration on the entries prefix is >= the Object Lock retention window (deletion only after lock expiry, §8)
- Pruning-checkpoint prefix excluded from lifecycle expiration (indefinite retention, §15.3)
- Replication configuration asserts Object Lock metadata is preserved (CRR, §15.3)
- Versioning enabled asserted (defense in depth, §8)

## Out of Scope
- Runtime deletion logic (prune-deletion-executor)
- LocalStack E2E validation (prune-objectlock-e2e)

## Testing
- CDK synth assertion tests (Jest); no cloud access

## Demo
`npm test` in the CDK package green; template diff shows lifecycle + Object Lock configuration.

tickets.title: Object Lock retention validated end-to-end on LocalStack
tickets.description:
## Goal
Deliver the Phase 7 obligation "Object Lock retention validated end-to-end" (§24): prove on LocalStack that Compliance-mode retention actually enforces append-only storage and that pruning respects it (§15.3, §8).

## Acceptance Criteria
- E2E suite: entries written via `put_with_retention` cannot be deleted before retain-until (delete attempt fails)
- With short dev retention + fake-clock advance (§18.4), the full pruning workflow runs and pruned entries are removed only after expiry
- Pruning checkpoints survive all pruning runs (indefinite retention, §15.3)
- Multi-region sim (`make demo-multiregion`, §18.3): replicated objects retain Object Lock attributes across simulated CRR
- Suite gated behind `--features integration` (§19.1) and wired into CI integration lane

## Out of Scope
- CDK synth assertions (prune-cdk-lifecycle)
- CLI-driven scenario test (prune-e2e-demo)

## Testing
- Integration + E2E against LocalStack (single-region and multi-region sim)

## Demo
`make demo` then `cargo test --features integration -p pruning objectlock_e2e` — output shows denied-before/allowed-after deletion transcript.
deps: EXTERNAL:fake-clock time-advance control (make time-advance, spec 18.4, local-dev-experience epic)
EXTERNAL:multi-region simulated environment (make demo-multiregion, spec 18.3, local-dev-experience epic)

tickets.title: Property tests: pruning preserves proofs for unpruned entries
tickets.description:
## Goal
Implement the §19.2 invariant: "Pruning a range and verifying a proof for an unpruned entry still works," plus tile-retention sufficiency (§15.2: interior nodes retained naturally by tile structure).

## Acceptance Criteria
- proptest strategy generates trees of arbitrary size, applies planner-produced pruned ranges, then asserts inclusion proofs verify for every unpruned index
- Negative control: removing a tile the planner marked as retained causes proof verification to fail (demonstrates the retained set is tight and necessary)
- Shrunk counterexamples from any failure captured as permanent regression fixtures (§19.3 corpus discipline)
- Runs in the fast unit lane (<30s, §19.1) with bounded case counts; extended case count behind a feature/env flag

## Out of Scope
- Planner implementation changes (prune-planner) beyond bug fixes the tests surface

## Testing
- Property (proptest), unit regression fixtures

## Demo
`cargo test -p ca-pruning proof_preservation` green; run with `PROPTEST_CASES=10000` for the extended sweep.

tickets.title: mtcctl prune status/run + admin API endpoints via OpenAPI
tickets.description:
## Goal
Expose pruning to operators per §17.3: `mtcctl prune status` (watermark + pending work) and `mtcctl prune run` (trigger workflow, privileged), backed by admin API routes defined in the OpenAPI spec so CLI and UI share one boundary (§17.1, §17.2, §17.5).

## Acceptance Criteria
- OpenAPI paths for prune status and prune run; generated client consumed by the CLI (no hand-rolled HTTP)
- `prune status` shows current watermark, last pruning checkpoint, and planner dry-run pending-work summary; supports `--output json` (§17.3)
- `prune run` is privileged: requires `--confirm` or interactive confirmation, skippable with `--yes` (§17.3); triggers a workflow execution, returns execution id; call recorded for the admin-actions audit log (§20.3)
- Sensible errors when standby (not primary) or when nothing is prunable
- UI can consume the same endpoints (data shape documented); UI tile itself is admin-surface epic work

## Out of Scope
- Admin UI rendering of pruning watermark (admin-surface epic)
- Workflow internals

## Testing
- Unit (route handlers on memory backend), integration (CLI against demo env), E2E smoke

## Demo
`make demo`; `mtcctl prune status`; `mtcctl prune run --yes` then `mtcctl prune status` shows advanced watermark.

tickets.title: E2E scenario test: issue then prune via mtcctl in tests/e2e
tickets.description:
## Goal
Cover the pruning leg of the §19.1 demo scenario ("issue -> verify -> revoke -> prune") as an E2E test in `tests/e2e/` driving `mtcctl` against the full demo environment.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Script (shell or Rust per §19.1) that: issues certs, advances the fake clock past dev retention, runs `mtcctl prune run --yes`, and asserts the watermark advanced
- Asserts inclusion proofs for unpruned entries still verify via `mtcctl` after pruning
- Asserts pruned indices are reported as pruned: `mtcctl prune status` shows the watermark above them and a proof request for a pruned index fails with a clear pruned/gone status, not an internal error (§20.2 forensics direction)
- Wired into the CI integration/E2E lane; runs green from a clean `make demo`

## Out of Scope
- Revocation leg of the scenario (revocation epic)
- Object Lock semantics validation (prune-objectlock-e2e)

## Testing
- E2E (CLI-driven against demo env)

## Demo
`./tests/e2e/prune.sh` (or `make e2e-prune`) runs the full scenario and prints the before/after watermark.
deps: EXTERNAL:e2e test harness conventions in tests/e2e (testing-infrastructure epic, spec 19.1)
EXTERNAL:fake-clock time-advance control (make time-advance, spec 18.4, local-dev-experience epic)

tickets.title: Deterministic post-pruning fixture: make fixture-load name=post-pruning
tickets.description:
## Goal
Provide the `post-pruning` deterministic fixture promised in §18.5: a snapshot of LocalStack + DDB state after a pruning run, loadable for bug reproduction, performance testing, and demos.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `make fixture-load name=post-pruning` restores a state with a nonzero pruning watermark, at least one pruning checkpoint, pruned entry gaps, and intact tiles for unpruned proofs
- Fixture generation is scripted and reproducible (regenerate from seed, not hand-edited blobs)
- After load, `mtcctl prune status` and proof verification for an unpruned entry both succeed
- Fixture documented alongside the other fixtures (§18.5)
- Used by at least one integration or E2E test as its starting state

## Out of Scope
- Fixture snapshot/restore infrastructure itself (local-dev-experience epic)

## Testing
- Integration smoke: load fixture, assert expected watermark and object layout

## Demo
`make fixture-load name=post-pruning` then `mtcctl prune status` shows the fixture's watermark instantly — no long pruning run needed.

tickets.title: Runbook: pruning failure (docs/runbooks/pruning-failure.md)
tickets.description:
## Goal
Write the required "pruning failure" runbook (§21.2) in `docs/runbooks/` following the standard structure: detection, initial assessment, mitigation, recovery, postmortem template.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Covers concrete failure modes: workflow stuck/failed mid-execution, deletion blocked by unexpired Object Lock at scale, watermark/checkpoint mismatch, pruning-checkpoint signing failure, replication-precondition stall
- Detection section names the alerts/metrics that fire (cross-referencing prune-metrics-events)
- Mitigation/recovery steps use real commands (`mtcctl prune status`, `mtcctl prune run`, workflow execution inspection) and were each executed once against the demo env with an induced failure
- Postmortem template included per §21.2

## Out of Scope
- Alert wiring itself (observability epic); metric emission (prune-metrics-events)

## Testing
- Docs lint/link check in CI; one manual walkthrough of recovery steps against demo env recorded in the PR description

## Demo
Induce a failure in demo env (kill workflow mid-run), then follow the runbook to recovery; watermark ends consistent.

tickets.title: Pruning watermark metric, workflow metrics, and compliance event exposure
tickets.description:
## Goal
Emit the pruning signals the observability surface depends on: always-visible pruning watermark (§20.2 dashboards, tree visualization), workflow outcome metrics, and queryable pruning event records feeding the Pruning log compliance report (§20.3).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Watermark gauge metric plus per-run metrics: duration, entries pruned, entries skipped (unexpired lock), result status
- Pruning event records written by the commit step (prune-commit-protocol) are queryable in the shape the compliance reporter needs — "All pruning events with affected ranges" (§20.3)
- Admin API exposes watermark and recent pruning events so the UI tree visualization can render the pruning watermark (§20.2)
- Metrics emitted in the demo env and visible via the local metrics endpoint

## Out of Scope
- Dashboards, SLOs, alert definitions, report generation (observability epic)
- UI rendering (admin-surface epic)

## Testing
- Unit (event record shape, metric emission), integration (demo env: run workflow, assert metrics/events present)

## Demo
`make demo`; trigger a prune; local metrics endpoint shows the watermark gauge move and a new pruning event record via the admin API.
